claims.text: A two-phase coexistence method within DFT-based molecular dynamics can estimate the melting temperature of high-melting refractory materials accurately.
A two-phase coexistence method within DFT-based molecular dynamics can estimate the enthalpy and entropy of fusion accurately.
A two-phase coexistence method within DFT-based molecular dynamics can estimate the volume change at the melting point accurately.
Interface pinning can be used as an alternative to a direct two-phase coexistence setup for calculating these melting properties.
The proposed approach significantly reduces computational cost relative to full ab initio thermodynamic integration.
Interface pinning stabilizes the solid-liquid interface in a DFT-based molecular dynamics simulation.
Maintaining solid-liquid coexistence allows equilibrium between the solid and liquid phases to be observed directly.
Direct solid-liquid coexistence bypasses the need for full thermodynamic integration.
Bypassing full thermodynamic integration reduces the amount of required sampling.
Energy discontinuities associated with solid-liquid coexistence can be used to obtain latent melting properties.
Volume discontinuities associated with solid-liquid coexistence can be used to obtain the volume change at melting.
The proposed method retains DFT-level accuracy while lowering computational cost.
Finite system-size effects can impair equilibration or accuracy of the solid-liquid interface.
Slow kinetics near the melting point can cause inaccurate equilibration of the solid-liquid interface.
Extreme metastable states may not be captured by the proposed approach.
The efficiency improvement and error margins depend on the material system and simulation parameters.
